newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on economic worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on economic worries.

text.p: Thai stocks closed lower in thin trade on Monday after investors sold stocks across the board on continued concerns over Thailand's slow economic growth and lagging exports, brokers said.

The SET index, which moved sluggishly throughout the session, dropped for the third consecutive trading day, falling 5.34 points to 920.63 on 2.6 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index declined 0.49 point to 70.03.
"Investors were still worried about Thai exports figures and economic growth. They fear that the economy's slowdown would affect corporate earnings this year," a broker said.
The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday Thailand's exports in September were valued at 112.5 billion baht compared to 117.7 billion baht in August and 126.2 billion a year ago.
"Foreign investors continued selling today out of their concerns over the Thai economy," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of Sitca Investment and Securities.

The market was bearish in the morning as investors awaited November inflation figures, earlier scheduled to be announced by the commerce ministry in the afternoon. The ministry postponed the annoucement until Tuesday due to a the change in government. The new cabinet was sworn in on Sunday and began work on Monday.
